To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electromigration lifetime of aluminum metallization is a function of the current density, temperature, metallization thickness and grain size, the grain structure, and the presence of contaminants.
Electromigration tests should be performed at high current densities and at temperatures that are as close as possible to the actual operating temperature of the device under study.
the current density is the most important parameter in electromigration, the most important test structure is the single line, and the best test method is the current stressing method.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following areas: (1) the effect of current density on electromigration lifetime; (2) the role of temperature in determining the electromigration lifetime; and (3) the role of the grain structure of the metal films

the development of a test structure that can be used to measure the electromigration lifetime of a device, as well as with the development of an analytical model that will allow the use of this test structure to extrapolate the lifetime of a device.
the development of a new test structure and procedure that is designed to eliminate or minimize the various problems and uncertainties associated with electromigration testing.

there is not sufficient data to make a definitive statement about the validity of electromigration tests, but there is enough data to suggest that electromigration is not a problem for most devices, at least at present, and that the tests are probably valid for most purposes, at least at the present time.
electromigration is a serious problem that is not fully understood.
the present state of knowledge and understanding of electromigration is inadequate to permit the design of electromigration-resistant metallization.

the problems are real, the uncertainties are significant, and that the data base for electromigration is still very limited.

the test data are valid only when the test conditions are identical to the operating conditions.
